lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: theorems about parallelograms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: Remote interior angles 40° and 65°. Exterior angle?

steps: Exterior equals the sum of the remote interiors.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 45°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 62. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 31, and it is perpendicular to the third side
124, and it is parallel to the third side
31, and it is parallel to the third side
62, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.
The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 58°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 25° and 65°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 71°. Find the opposite angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 28. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 14, and it is perpendicular to the third side
28, and it is parallel to the third side
14, and it is parallel to the third side
56, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
